questions.question_text: A three-set diagram has Yellow-only 12, Pink-only 10, Green-only 11, Yellow∩Pink-only 9, Yellow∩Green-only 7, and all-three 8. How many are Pink but neither Green nor Yellow?
questions.explanation: ‘Neither Green nor Yellow’ excludes every overlap with either set. The Pink-only region in the diagram is labeled 10.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which relationship best represents Mango, Fruit and Cauliflower?

options.A: Mango is inside Fruit; Cauliflower is separate from both.
options.C: Fruit is inside Mango; Cauliflower is separate.
options.D: Mango and Cauliflower are inside Fruit and overlap each other.

questions.explanation: Every mango is a fruit, so Mango is a subset of Fruit. Cauliflower is not a fruit, so its set is separate from both in this classification.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which diagram best represents Wheat, Grains, Onion and Maize?

options.A: Wheat and Maize are separate subsets of Grains; Onion is outside Grains.
options.B: All four sets are completely disjoint.
options.C: Onion is inside Grains, while Wheat and Maize are outside.
options.D: Wheat, Grains and Maize form three nested sets; Onion overlaps them.

questions.explanation: Wheat and maize are kinds of grain, but neither is the other. Onion is not a grain, so it is disjoint from the Grains set.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 22; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which relationship best represents Vegetable, Woman, Lion and Parrot?

options.A: Four separate sets with no overlap.
options.B: Woman contains Vegetable; Lion and Parrot overlap.
options.C: Lion and Parrot are nested inside Vegetable.
options.D: All four sets overlap in one common region.

questions.explanation: These labels denote different classes: vegetables, people who are women, lions, and parrots. None is a subset of or overlaps another class in the intended classification diagram.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 23; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which diagram best represents Teachers, Parents and Guardians when people may belong to more than one group?

options.C: Three partially overlapping circles, including a possible common intersection.
options.D: Two overlapping circles and one separate circle.

questions.explanation: A person can be a teacher, a parent, and a guardian at the same time; each role can also occur without the other two. The sets therefore overlap and may share a common region, but none contains another.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 8; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In a Kesar/Mint/Vanilla diagram, the exclusive regions are: Kesar 32, Mint 21, Vanilla 45, Kesar-Mint 12, Kesar-Vanilla 14, Mint-Vanilla 20, and all three 10. How many people like Mint but not Kesar?
questions.explanation: Mint but not Kesar includes Mint only (21) and Mint-and-Vanilla only (20). Exclude both Kesar-and-Mint regions, including the all-three region. Thus 21 + 20 = 41.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A Clerks/Potters/Farmers diagram has exclusive regions: Clerks 20, Potters 23, Farmers 45, Clerks-Potters 12, Clerks-Farmers 9, Potters-Farmers 8, and all three 6. How many are both clerks and potters?
questions.explanation: The Clerks∩Potters total includes the Clerks-and-Potters-only region (12) and the all-three region (6): 12 + 6 = 18.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In a four-set diagram, the regions are Florists-only 23, Florists-Teachers 9, Teachers-only 34, Teachers-Celebrities 7, Celebrities-only 25, Celebrities-Doctors 13, and Doctors-only 56. How many are both teachers and florists?
questions.explanation: The shared Teachers∩Florists region is labeled 9. The value 7 belongs to Teachers∩Celebrities, a different overlap.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In an Urban/Male/Educated diagram, the exclusive regions are U-only 1, M-only 2, E-only 3, U-M 5, U-E 4, M-E 6, and all three 10. How many people belong to the Urban set?
questions.explanation: The Urban set includes Urban-only 1, Urban∩Male-only 5, Urban∩Educated-only 4, and the all-three region 10. Total = 1 + 5 + 4 + 10 = 20.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: For Hindi/English/French, the exclusive regions are H-only 20, E-only 10, F-only 20, H-E 25, H-F 10, E-F 10, and all three 10. How many people speak exactly one language?
questions.explanation: Exactly one language means the three single-language regions only: Hindi-only 20 + English-only 10 + French-only 20 = 50.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: For Hindi/English/French, the exclusive regions are H-only 20, E-only 10, F-only 20, H-E 25, H-F 10, E-F 10, and all three 10. How many people speak exactly two languages?
questions.explanation: Exactly two languages includes the three pair-only regions: 25 + 10 + 10 = 45. The triple-language region is not included.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: For Hindi/English/French, the exclusive regions are H-only 20, E-only 10, F-only 20, H-E 25, H-F 10, E-F 10, and all three 10. How many people speak all three languages?
questions.explanation: The central intersection of Hindi, English and French is labeled 10.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 20; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In a Boys/Athletes/College Students diagram, the exclusive regions are boys-only 7, boys-athletes 10, athletes-only 14, boys-college 12, athletes-college 6, college-only 15, and all three 9. How many boys are both college students and athletes?
questions.explanation: The question asks for Boys∩College Students∩Athletes, the central region common to all three circles. It is labeled 9.
questions.source: Venn Diagram 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 22; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: All surgeons are doctors. Some surgeons are men, some surgeons are not men, and some men are not doctors. Which diagram fits?

options.A: Surgeons inside Doctors; Men overlaps both and extends outside Doctors.
options.B: Doctors inside Surgeons; Men is separate.
options.D: Men contains both Doctors and Surgeons.

questions.explanation: Surgeons are wholly within Doctors. The stated examples require Men to overlap Surgeons and Doctors while also extending beyond Doctors; the non-men surgeons occupy a Doctors-and-Surgeons region outside Men.

questions.question_text: Patna is within Bihar, and Bihar is within India. Which diagram represents these classes?

options.D: Patna and Bihar overlap, while India is separate.

questions.explanation: Every location in Patna is in Bihar, and every location in Bihar is in India. The sets form a three-level containment chain.

questions.question_text: Gold and Silver are metals, and no object is classified as both Gold and Silver. Which diagram fits?

options.A: Gold and Silver are disjoint subsets inside Metals.
options.B: Metals is inside Gold; Silver overlaps it.
options.C: Gold, Silver and Metals are all disjoint.
options.D: Gold is inside Silver inside Metals.

questions.explanation: Both Gold and Silver belong to the broader Metals class. They are distinct, non-overlapping classes, so draw two disjoint subsets within Metals.

questions.question_text: Pet cats and pet dogs are both pet animals, and no animal in this question is both a cat and a dog. Pet animals are animals. Which diagram fits?

options.A: Pet cats and pet dogs are disjoint subsets of Pet Animals, inside Animals.
options.B: Animals inside Pet Animals inside Pet Cats.
options.C: Pet Cats and Pet Dogs overlap; Animals is separate.

questions.explanation: Both pet categories are contained within Pet Animals, which is within Animals. The question states pet cats and pet dogs are disjoint.

questions.question_text: Some A are B. Some B are C. No A is C. Which diagram is possible?

options.A: A and C are disjoint; each overlaps B in separate regions.
options.B: A, B and C are completely disjoint.
options.C: A is inside C, and both are inside B.
options.D: All three share one common region.

questions.explanation: The premises require an A∩B region and a separate B∩C region, while A and C never intersect. Thus B overlaps each of two mutually disjoint sets.

questions.question_text: All students and all athletes are people. Some students are athletes, some students are not athletes, and some athletes are not students. Which diagram fits?

options.A: Students and Athletes partially overlap inside People.
options.B: Students and Athletes are disjoint inside People.
options.C: Students are inside Athletes, both inside People.
options.D: People is inside the overlap of Students and Athletes.

questions.explanation: Both sets are subsets of People. The examples establish a nonempty intersection and nonempty parts unique to each set, so the two sets partially overlap inside People.

questions.question_text: Some teachers are singers, some students are singers, and some singers belong to neither group. No teacher is a student. Which diagram fits?

options.A: Teachers and Students are disjoint; each overlaps Singers in separate regions.
options.B: Teachers, Students and Singers all overlap in a common center.
options.C: Teachers are inside Students; Singers is separate.
options.D: Teachers and Students overlap, while Singers is disjoint from both.

questions.explanation: Teachers and Students must be disjoint. Their stated singer members make Singers overlap each set in separate regions, while the singer-only region is nonempty.

questions.question_text: All apples are fruits, and no vegetable is a fruit. Which diagram represents Apples, Fruits and Vegetables?

options.A: Apples inside Fruits; Vegetables separate from Fruits.
options.B: Fruits inside Apples; Vegetables overlap Fruits.
options.D: Apples and Vegetables are inside Fruits.

questions.explanation: Apples form a subset of Fruits. Vegetables are disjoint from Fruits, so they are also disjoint from Apples.

questions.question_text: In a survey, 46 people chose A, 39 chose B, and 17 chose both. How many chose at least one of A or B?
questions.explanation: The inclusive totals count the 17 in both twice. Union = 46 + 39 − 17 = 68.

questions.question_text: Of 150 people, 86 drink tea, 72 drink coffee, and 28 drink neither. How many drink both tea and coffee?
questions.explanation: At least one = 150 − 28 = 122. By inclusion-exclusion, both = 86 + 72 − 122 = 36.

questions.question_text: In a class, 72 study Mathematics, 58 study Science, and 31 study both. How many study Science only?
questions.explanation: Science-only members are the Science total minus those in both subjects: 58 − 31 = 27.

questions.question_text: Of 90 people, 55 belong to A and 48 to B. If 78 belong to at least one set, how many belong to exactly one set?
questions.explanation: The intersection is 55 + 48 − 78 = 25. Exactly one = (55 − 25) + (48 − 25) = 53.

questions.question_text: A group has 64 members in A, 51 in B, and 27 in both. How many are in A only?
questions.explanation: A-only excludes the intersection: 64 − 27 = 37.

questions.question_text: Set A has 75 members. The inclusive totals are A∩B=30 and A∩C=25, while A∩B∩C=10. How many are in A only?
questions.explanation: Within A, the inclusive AB and AC counts double-count the 10 in all three. A-only = 75 − 30 − 25 + 10 = 30.

questions.question_text: In a survey of 240 people, A=110, B=100, C=90; inclusive AB=40, AC=35, BC=30; all three=15. How many belong to none of the sets?
A survey diagram shows A-only 10, B-only 12, C-only 8, AB-only 4, AC-only 3, BC-only 5, all three 2, and outside all sets 6. How many are neither A nor C?
questions.explanation: Neither A nor C includes the B-only region (12) and the region outside all sets (6). Total = 12 + 6 = 18.

questions.question_text: Three sets have disjoint region counts: A-only 14, B-only 11, C-only 9, AB-only 6, AC-only 5, BC-only 4, and all three 3. How many belong to at least one set?
questions.explanation: At least one means the union: add all seven mutually exclusive regions. 14 + 11 + 9 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 52.
